subject: Intermittent 503s & p99 tail regressions affecting NovusAI - urgent
messages:
From: Alyssa Chen <alyssa.chen@novus.ai>
To: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>
Cc: ops@novus.ai
Date: Wed, 09 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Intermittent 503s & p99 tail regressions impacting Novus search - urgent

Hi Olga,

We started seeing a spike in 5xx rates and p95/p99 tail latency across our search endpoints around 09:05 PDT this morning. Error rate went from ~0.2% to 6% over a 12 minute window; p99 jumped from ~480ms to 3.2s. We also observed short-lived 503s for ~2% of requests. The issue correlates with requests routed to your hosted endpoints for model: redwood/large-search-v2.

Attached a sample request trace (request-trace-20270609.json) and our internal alert graph. We suspect something on the inference side — please escalate. This is impacting production customers and search latency SLA.

Requested info:
- Any known runtime incidents or maintenance?
- Temporary mitigation we can flip from our side?
- ETA for a diagnosis & mitigation plan?

We can provide traffic slices if useful.

Thanks,
Alyssa
Alyssa Chen
SRE Lead, NovusAI
ops@novus.ai

Subject: Re: Intermittent 503s & p99 tail regressions impacting Novus search - urgent

Olga / team — quick triage notes after looking at the attached traces and runtime logs:

Observed signals:
- Multiple allocation failures (OOMs) in GPU allocator logs at 09:06–09:09 followed by retries and request timeouts.
- Fragmentation pattern: small free slabs scattered across memory with large contiguous allocation requests failing.
- KV cache growth for redwood/large-search-v2: a small subset of long-lived keys (likely rare cached prefixes) ballooned in resident set due to changes in prefix hits; eviction frequency dropped.

Hypothesis: GPU memory fragmentation (slab splitting + infrequent eviction) leading to transient OOMs. When an allocation path fails we see p99 blow up and some 503s as requests are retried/failfast. Not classic model weight OOM.

Immediate mitigations (I can execute now if we agree):
1) Purge KV cache for affected model shard(s) (non-disruptive) — should reclaim fragmented regions quickly.
2) Temporarily reduce max sequence length to 512 for your traffic route to reduce peak allocation requests.
3) Patch allocator flags to prefer defragmenting allocations (safe change, small kernel tweak) and roll to a subset of nodes for canary.
4) Emergency autoscale: +20% capacity to reduce queueing while we stabilize.

Longer-term follow-ups:
- Add eviction aggressiveness tuning and fragmentation-aware compaction in runtime.
- Postmortem to capture traffic patterns that triggered KV growth and add guardrails (per-tenant cache caps).

If you want, I'll start the KV purge and capacity bump now — estimate 8–12 minutes to see improvement in tail latencies.

— Rishi
Rishi Malhotra
Principal SRE, Runtime Reliability
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Intermittent 503s & p99 tail regressions impacting Novus search - urgent

Rolling the agreed mitigations now:
- Initiated KV cache purge for model shard ID shard-17 (affected pool).
- Bumped autoscale target for pool redwood-hosted-xy to +25% capacity.
- Applied a canary allocator flag change on 4 nodes; observing stability before wider rollout.
- Temporarily capped seq_len at 512 for NovusAI route (config applied, will revert after 2 hours if stable).

Initial observations (09:40 PDT): p99 reduced from 3.2s -> ~620ms; 5xx rate dropping toward baseline. Will continue to monitor and collect heap/alloc dumps for postmortem.

Eviction log attached.

— Diego

Subject: Customer update: mitigation in place & next steps (NovusAI)

Alyssa — quick update for your team and customers:

What happened (short):
- We observed GPU allocator failures driven by memory fragmentation tied to unusual KV cache growth for your model shard. That caused transient OOMs and request failures, which surfaced as p99 spikes and some 503s.

What we did (now):
- Purged the KV cache for the affected shard.
- Applied a temporary seq_len cap (512) for your route.
- Rolled a small allocator flag change as a canary and increased pool capacity (+25%).

Current status: tail latency and error rate are back within acceptable bounds (p99 ~580–700ms, 5xx trending to baseline). We'll keep monitoring for 2 hours.

Next steps / follow-up:
- We'll run a focused postmortem and share findings within 72 hours.
- Engineering follow-ups include fragmentation-aware compaction, per-tenant cache caps, and an allocator improvement rollout.

Compensation / credits: Marissa will follow up on account-level credits given the SLA impact (cc'd).

If you can, please share any request IDs or traffic patterns from 09:00–09:15 to help root cause.

Apologies again for the disruption — we appreciate your patience.

Best,
Olga Petrov
Account Manager, Customer Success
Redwood Inference
